title: Site Model — registry/services.yml
description: One record per service. Every launchd plist, systemd unit, and Termux/mise agent is a rendering of one such record (§4.1). CFEngine owns services on every platform (D13/§5.3), so `managed_by` is `cfengine` for anything under management.

domains.description: Coverage declaration per domain of device state this file describes (D16(d)). Keys are domain ids referenced by each service record.

bundles.description: Grouping AND re-verification scope (D16(c)): entries in a bundle are validated collectively, all members are reverified when any one is modified, and services in a bundle are restarted when any member changes.

name.description: Unique across the file. This is the id `depends_on` refers to.

domain.description: Must be a key in the top-level `domains`. Cross-checked by bin/schema_lint.py.

bundle.description: Must be a key in the top-level `bundles`. Determines the interlock blast radius and the re-verify scope.

hosts.description: Hosts this service is declared on. Omit for role-bound services — the role's assignment in roles.yml decides.

role.description: Feature role from roles.yml. This is what dissolves 'control node' into data (R2).

runs_as.description: Local user the service runs as.

command.description: argv, not a shell string — a shell string would put quoting rules between the model and the renderer.

managed_by.description: Who writes this service's on-device definition. `cfengine` for anything under management (D13/§5.3); the others exist so reality can be transcribed truthfully before it is migrated.

label.description: Must fall under a prefix declared in launchd-writers.yml — cross-checked by bin/schema_lint.py. This is the lint that makes Step 1 survivable on a live daily driver.

then.$comment: A macOS service with no launchd label cannot be checked against launchd-writers.yml, which is the whole two-writers safety rail.
